newsitem.title: USA: Tandem CEO sees new product benefit in FY 97.
newsitem.headline: Tandem CEO sees new product benefit in FY 97.

text.p: Tandem Computers Inc chief executive Roel Pieper said he expects financial benefits from the company's new servers in fiscal 1997, because many of its customers have shown interest in its new products.
Earlier, Tandem introduced two new lines of server computers, one using its own Himilayan architecture running the UNIX operating system and a new lower-cost line running Microsoft Corp's Windows NT.
"They would be very clearly interested in this," Pieper said after a press conference here. He said Tandem did a poll and 70 percent of its customers would use Windows NT servers.
"We take the Windows NT opportunity very seriously," Pieper said. "I'd say that our NT business opportunity is at least a $1 billion plus business."
Pieper said that, if Tandem is successful in this market, it could reach that goal in NT sales in three to four years, but he declined to make any projections.

Tandem's foray into the Windows NT server market marks the first time is has embraced the Microsoft/Intel architecture. The four S-Series servers running Windows NT use Intel Corp Pentium Pro processors and begin at $10,000 for the basic configuration.
Tandem's two new Himalaya S-Series servers begin at $60,000 and are twice as powerful as its current offerings.
Pieper declined to be more specific on what Tandem expects in terms of revenues from the new products in fiscal 1997.

Tandem also said it made a strategic investment in a small company called Interval Inc of $1.2 million, which is developing software for the rights management of digital content of public networks and for secure electronic payment.
Tandem also formed a joint venture with Planet Hollywood Intl and Informix Corp, to work on developing a strategy for digital rights management.
